title: Posterior-regret trace-cap converse for blind quantum or hybrid archives
theorem: Let X have law mu, let a blind encoder map x to a state rho_x on a D-dimensional Hilbert space, and let a fixed query decoder use a POVM M(dy) with bounded regret 0<=R(x,y)<=L. For a measurable chart C of mass m and V(u)=sup_y mu({x in C:R(x,y)<=u}), E R(X,Y)>=integral_0^L [m-D V(u)]_+ du. For direct-sum hybrid memory D=sum_j d_j. Independent public seeds are allowed if every seed uses dimension at most D.
proof: rho_x<=I_D implies integral_{C_y}rho_x dmu<=V(u)I_D. Integrating against the POVM gives Pr[X in C,R<=u]<=D V(u); integrate the complementary tail in u.
costs: D counts all quantum blocks and all dephased classical labels; bits are log2(D). Decoder/runtime, precision and output costs are outside the inequality and must be reported separately.
baseline: A classical quantizer has the same trace-cap upper bound; equality requires a separate positive reference-preserving codec.
falsifier: A finite-dimensional blind code violating the displayed integrated bound under the stated POVM interface.
unresolved_gate: External proof and priority review; determine when a matching positive codec exists for a specified family.

title: Independent later queries pay a sum of scalar rate-distortion costs
theorem: For independent classical features X_1,...,X_d encoded before the query into one D-dimensional quantum/hybrid memory M, if query i may use its own POVM and guarantees distortion at most delta_i, then ln D >= sum_i R_i(delta_i), where R_i is the scalar Shannon rate-distortion function under that query's distortion.
proof: For each i, measurement data processing gives I(X_i;Y_i)<=I(X_i;M). Independence and strong subadditivity give sum_i I(X_i;M)<=I(X_1...X_d;M)<=ln D. Since R_i(delta_i)<=I(X_i;Y_i), sum the inequalities. No joint measurement of incompatible query outputs is assumed.
costs: All hybrid branch dimensions are charged through D. Query descriptions and measurements are external; charge their communication/runtime if the application requires it.
baseline: Classical product rate-distortion code with the same feature priors and distortions.
falsifier: A counterexample to conditional-entropy subadditivity/Holevo under this finite-dimensional interface or an archive beating the Shannon lower bound.
unresolved_gate: The source-derived N36/N66 specializations need external proof review; the theorem does not apply to dependent features or encoder-known queries.

title: Fisher information alone cannot determine one-shot archive cost
theorem: On theta in [pi/3,2pi/3], X~N(theta,1) and X~Bernoulli(sin^2(theta/2)) have identical Fisher information 1 for every theta. The Bernoulli observation is stored exactly with D=2; D=1 has worst-case TV error at least 1/4. Under the source-derived N07 Gaussian rate for affine dimension one, e_D=Theta(D^-2), so D_min(epsilon)=Theta(epsilon^-1/2).
proof: For Bernoulli, p'(theta)^2/(p(1-p))=1. The endpoints have Bernoulli TV distance 1/2, so one fixed output law has radius at least 1/4. Store the observed bit for exact reconstruction. The Gaussian conclusion is N07's affine-dimension-one theorem, not independently externally validated here.
supplied_inputs: known scalar family and parameter interval
costs: Bernoulli D=2 means one archive bit; Gaussian bits grow as (1/2)log2(1/epsilon)+O(1). Ideal continuous output is assumed for the Gaussian claim.
baseline: Store the Bernoulli symbol exactly; use the Gaussian positive-hat archive from N07 for the continuous source.
falsifier: A proof that the two archive orders coincide under the stated TV interface, or a counterexample to the one-dimensional N07 rate.
unresolved_gate: The Gaussian half inherits N07's source-derived internal status; no universal compression law from the full Fisher metric follows.

title: Known-spectrum near-tracial qudit orbit has a partial-collision leading profile
theorem: Fix d and known sorted p_n in [1/(2d),3/(2d)]^d with p_n->I/d. Set B_n=product_{i<j}(1+n(p_{n,i}-p_{n,j})^2), H_n=log2(B_n), and delta_n=1-product_{i<j}(p_{n,j}/p_{n,i}). A total hybrid memory D=sum_j d_j that reconstructs the entire n-copy state with half-trace error <=1/8 has D>=c_d B_n. A candidate classical archive has D<=C_d eta^{-2(d^2-1)}B_n and error <=delta_n+eta. If H_n->infinity, vanishing-error leading cost is H_n+o(H_n). For prescribed epsilon_n, the upper is certified if epsilon_n>delta_n eventually and log2(1/(epsilon_n-delta_n))=o(H_n); this is sufficient, not known necessary.
proof: The independent lower uses only the one-sided closed-chamber orbital-integral bound, a maximal Frobenius net, fixed informationally complete tomography with O_d(1/n) risk, and the total-hybrid trace cap; it proves D>=c_{d,e}B_n for every fixed error e<1. The upper's Schur/coherent likelihood, weighted-flag chart and positive code are reconstructed from an earlier internal candidate package; those analytic steps have not been externally certified.
acquired_inputs: none; spectrum and model are supplied
costs: All hybrid branches count via D=sum_j d_j. The theorem is information-theoretic; gates, runtime, source acquisition, precision, decoder randomness and fresh n-qudit output are separate.
baseline: The same known-spectrum classical whole-state archive; the lower permits arbitrary quantum/hybrid memory.
falsifier: A code below c_d B_n at error <=1/8, or a counterexample to the weighted-flag upper within the stated band.
proof_location: work/programmes/memory_information/leaves/collision_scalings.txt, sections 1-5; independent lower at work/programmes/memory_information/leaves/collision_lower_independent.txt; exact fixtures in outputs/research/memory_information/evidence/collision_scalings/
unresolved_gate: Upper proof reuses internal prior machinery; independent proof audit and the exact prescribed-epsilon optimum remain open. No unknown-spectrum acquisition is included.

title: Collision product is not a complete law at critical precision or uniformly in growing d
theorem: The all-accuracy extension D=Theta(B_n) for every vanishing-error sequence is false: for n=k^2 and qubit spectrum (1/2+3/(2k),1/2-3/(2k)), B_n=10 but every archive with bounded total hybrid dimension along a subsequence has error bounded away from zero. A dimension-uniform extension is also false: for d=n and p=(1-eta,eta/(d-1),...), eta=epsilon/(16n), a symmetric-subspace archive uses D=binom(n+d-1,n) with error <=epsilon/8, while log2 B_n=(n-1)log2(n)+O(1) and log2 D<=2n-1.
proof: The critical-qubit lower forms m=D0^2+1 distinct phase queries and a Vandermonde matrix of true expectations whose limiting matrix has full rank m; every decoded expectation matrix through D0-dimensional memory has rank at most D0^2. The growing-d upper projects onto Sym^n(C^d); the n-copy state is within trace distance <=n eta of the dominant pure orbit, which this subspace reconstructs exactly. The pure symmetric dimension is binom(n+d-1,n).
supplied_inputs: critical qubit: known full orbit spectrum and whole-state reconstruction
growing d: known near-rank-one full-rank spectrum, unknown eigenbasis
costs: D is total Hilbert dimension, archive bits log2 D. Symmetric-subspace gates and growing-d compiler/runtime are not included; output generation is separate.
baseline: Exact spin-sector/Sym^n storage with the same family promise; the latter is established pure-state compression prior art.
falsifier: A bounded-D sequence for the critical qubit with vanishing whole-state trace error, or a uniform-in-d lower c B_n for the displayed near-pure family.
unresolved_gate: The fixed-d collision theorem is not refuted; find a corrected profile involving precision, rank/tail mass, and representation-space cap.

title: Pure rank boundary removes one counted cutoff factor
theorem: For N23's local qubit family at known lambda=0, fixed R, blind total-hybrid dimension D=sum_j d_j, and uniform half-trace reconstruction error epsilon, a Dicke cutoff gives D<=O_R(1+min(n,h_epsilon)), h_epsilon=ln(1/epsilon)/ln ln(1/epsilon), with no epsilon*n restriction. Hence a square lower bound uniform over lambda>=0 is false. The matching two-sided pure-face optimum is only SOURCE-REPORTED via N22.
proof: The Dicke excitation B is binomial with n p<=R^2. For m>=1, E[(B)_m]<=(R^2)^m and P(B>=m)<=(R^2)^m/m!. A good m-dimensional quantum branch plus one charged failure label has trace error <=sqrt(t)+t; when m>n, store the exact n+1-dimensional symmetric block.
costs: Total D includes the dephased failure branch; public cutoff control bits and arithmetic are listed separately. No z estimate, retained real parameter, input flag, or free failure label.
baseline: Exact symmetric-subspace storage D=n+1; the cutoff archive improves it to min(n,h_epsilon) order.
falsifier: An explicit archive violating the factorial-tail bound or a uniform square lower bound on the lambda=0 face.
unresolved_gate: N22's detailed matching lower is absent locally; fixed-positive-Lambda finite-n total-D lower below the C/n bridge remains open.

title: Unknown inverse geometry defeats a law based only on singular values
theorem: Let A_i=r e_i e_1^T, i=1,...,d, all having singular values (r,0,...,0). If the encoder sees X~N(+/-r e_i,I_d) without i and receives the coordinate query i only after storage, the N36 lower gives ln D >= (d/2)ln(r/epsilon)-(5/4+ln2)d for 128 epsilon<=r<=1. When i is known before storage, a scalar positive-hat code costs (1/2)log2(r/epsilon)+O(1) bits. Thus geometry/query acquisition changes the leading precision coefficient by d although every operator's singular spectrum is identical.
proof: Reduce A_i(+/-e_1)=+/-r e_i exactly to N36's Gaussian needle interface. The inherited N36 proof uses bounded proper loss, independent reference coordinates, strong subadditivity and a separate Holevo inequality per later query. The upper is a product of reference-preserving Gaussian hats.
supplied_inputs: known family of possible rank-one maps but hidden active direction i
acquired_inputs: the active geometry is not acquired by the encoder; the query supplies i to the decoder after storage
costs: All hybrid archive dimensions count. Query communication, matrix/basis calibration, public tables, precision, fresh Gaussian output and runtime are separate. Continuous output is idealized.
baseline: Same Gaussian noise and r with i supplied before encoding; one scalar classical archive is the matched baseline.
falsifier: A blind shared archive of dimension below the N36 bound that answers every later i-specific POVM under the stated TV guarantee.
unresolved_gate: The N36 bound is source-derived and not independently externally validated; no unknown-basis calibration lower/upper is proved.

title: Fixed-reference QLAN covers unitary-orbit degeneracies but not moving collisions
theorem: Yamaguchi--Tajima arXiv:2609.11926v2, Part III, gives strong two-way trace-norm QLAN for the unitary orbit of one fixed finite-d density matrix, allowing repeated positive eigenvalues and rank deficiency. It treats horizontal rotations between distinct spectral blocks and has a remainder O(n^(-1/2+kappa)) in its stated local parameter range, with constants depending on the fixed reference spectrum/gaps.
proof: The paper constructs typical-Schur-sector isometries from truncated Fock modes tensor a ground component E_lambda, traces/reprepares E_lambda in the channels, and proves trace-norm approximation. It contains no unknown within-block splitting coordinates and no uniform triangular-gap estimate.
costs: This is an experiment-equivalence theorem, not by itself a finite-bit archive rate. QLAN map construction costs, spectrum acquisition, and finite-n decoder costs are not covered here.
baseline: Kahn--Guța (2009) fixed simple faithful spectrum QLAN; Yamaguchi--Tajima extends fixed-orbit multiplicities/rank, not triangular collisions.
falsifier: A reading of the primary theorem showing it includes n-dependent closing gaps or arbitrary within-block spectral perturbations.
proof_location: work/programmes/memory_information/leaves/primary_literature_collision.txt, section 1 and proof detail; source record https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11926
unresolved_gate: Joint block-splitting and transverse-rotation channel with explicit uniform gap-dependent remainder; fixed-reference constants do not transfer to p_n with shrinking gaps.

title: Common-eigenbasis spectral perturbations have an explicit n-copy stability bound
theorem: For fixed d, parameter set Theta_n, common unitary U_{n,theta}, spectra p_{n,theta},q_{n,theta} with supp(p) subset supp(q), and Xi_n=sup_theta sum_{i:q_i>0}(p_i-q_i)^2/q_i, the n-copy trace distance is uniformly at most r_n=min{1,sqrt(n Xi_n/2)}. For the same later-query archive interface, |e_D(E_n^p)-e_D(E_n^q)|<=2r_n. A transfer of the N08 bridge requires eta_n+2r_n=o(epsilon_n).
proof: Quantum relative entropy is invariant under the common U and additive on tensor powers: D(rho_p^tensor n||rho_q^tensor n)=nD(p||q). The classical inequality D(p||q)<=chi^2(p||q), followed by quantum Pinsker, gives the state bound. Contractivity moves both the decoded output and target output, giving 2r_n for the archive risk curve.
supplied_inputs: same known or unknown unitary parameter U in both models
p support contained in q support
costs: The comparison itself uses no storage but does not acquire p or q. Spectrum estimation/description and the archive code remain separate. The bound may be too large when n chi-square is not small.
baseline: Compare to the known reference spectrum q and transfer its archive by the triangle inequality.
falsifier: A violation of tensor-product relative-entropy additivity, D<=chi-square, or Pinsker under the stated half-trace convention.
unresolved_gate: This is only a closeness lemma, not QLAN and not the full partial-collision archive law; no converse follows when n Xi_n is large.

title: A shrinking unknown rare-rank interval inherits the pure-face memory order
theorem: For the N23 local-qubit family with known n,R, unknown z and intensity lambda in [0,Lambda_n], if Lambda_n<=epsilon_n/2 and n>=4Lambda_n, then the full n-copy state is uniformly within half-trace distance Lambda_n of the lambda=0 pure face at the same z. A pure-face archive at tolerance epsilon_n/2 gives D=O_R(1+min(n,h_{epsilon_n/2})); the lambda=0 subfamily gives the matching order lower through N22, whose detailed lower proof is source-reported rather than independently replayed. Thus the source-reported two-sided order is Theta_R(1+min(n,h_{epsilon_n})) even when epsilon_n<<1/n.
proof: For each fixed z, the rank-one target projector is an eigenvector of the one-copy state with eigenvalue 1-lambda/n. Its overlap with the tensor-power state is (1-lambda/n)^n, so the pure-target half-trace distance is exactly 1-(1-lambda/n)^n<=lambda<=Lambda_n. Compose with the pure-face archive and use the triangle inequality. Restricting to lambda=0 imports N22 lower.
supplied_inputs: same z used in the pure and mixed family
acquired_inputs: none; z and lambda remain unknown to the encoder
costs: Total hybrid dimension D charges all branches. No additional intensity estimation is used. Decoder runtime, precision, and output preparation remain separate.
baseline: Pure-face Dicke cutoff archive with its same blind uniform-z contract.
falsifier: An allowed mixed state farther than Lambda_n from the corresponding pure face, or an archive violating the N22 lower on the included lambda=0 subfamily.
unresolved_gate: N22 detailed total-D lower remains source-reported; no matching finite-n total-D lower is established for a fixed positive Lambda below the C/n bridge.

title: Critical iid-qubit orbits have a sharp-order EB reconstruction floor
theorem: Fix 0<c0<=c1<infinity. For known 0<r<=1/2 with c0<=r*sqrt(n)<=c1 and unknown v in S^2, require full n-qubit density reconstruction in worst-case half trace distance. Every entanglement-breaking channel, including arbitrary outcome spaces and arbitrary input/output Schur-sector transitions, has error e>=c(c0,c1)r. A coherent measure-and-prepare channel has e<=2r and can be made finite with all labels charged. Hence the optimum EB error is Theta_(c0,c1)(r)=Theta_(c0,c1)(n^(-1/2)).
proof: The exact Schur reduction gives known sector probabilities P_L and thermal spin states tau_(L,v). For spin j=L/2, the covariant first-harmonic identity bounds the norm of every measurement posterior direction by a_L=Tr(tau_(L,z)J_z)/(j+1). A bounded quadratic score F_K(v)=a_K(v.J_K/j_K)-a_K^2 I/2 has global interval [-3/2,1/2] using a_K<=1. For any input posterior sector L and prepared output sector K, completing the square gives decoded score <=a_L^2/2, whereas the target score is a_L^2/2+a_L^2/j_L. Haar averaging and half-trace duality yield e>=sum_L P_L a_L^2/L. A uniform positive critical mass window 2/r<=L<=B/r has a_L>=1/3, giving e>=c r. The coherent EB channel gives e<=2r.
supplied_inputs: unknown full SU(2) orbit direction v
full-state reconstruction and worst-case half-trace metric
costs: The converse covers all classical outcome spaces and therefore all EB alphabets. A finite coherent implementation has a finite label count. The theorem concerns EB error, not optimal total hybrid dimension or minimum quantum branch size. Decoder runtime, precision, gates, and fresh output preparation remain separate.
baseline: The same full-orbit family with known r; coherent EB reconstruction is the matching order upper baseline.
falsifier: An EB reconstruction channel within the stated interface with worst-case half-trace error o(r) along a critical sequence, or a failure of the posterior-score inequality under an allowed sector-changing output.
proof_location: outputs/research/sol_collision_precision/RESULT.txt, sections 6 and 12-13; exact finite checks in outputs/research/sol_collision_precision/evidence/; targeted ancestry audit in outputs/research/memory_information/prior_art_critical_eb.md
unresolved_gate: Independent proof audit and priority review remain open; the targeted search found close posterior-direction and spin-twirl ancestors but is not a novelty certificate. The minimum quantum branch dimension for error o(r) and the sharp total hybrid memory law remain UNKNOWN.

title: Critical qubit full-state error trades inversely with maximum quantum branch dimension
theorem: For known 0<r<=1/2 with c0<=r*sqrt(n)<=c1 and unknown v in S^2, let e_Q be the minimax worst-case half-trace error for full reconstruction of rho_(r,v)^tensor n by a dephased hybrid memory whose every quantum branch has dimension at most Q; classical outcomes are unrestricted in the converse. There are constants c,C>0 depending only on c0,c1 such that c*r/Q<=e_Q<=C*r/Q for integers 1<=Q<=1/(32r), for sufficiently small r. The same radius-independent encoder gives worst-case error O(c1/(sqrt(n)Q)) on the unknown-radius ball ||b||<=c1/sqrt(n), and restriction to a fixed critical sphere gives a matching lower for Q up to a constant times sqrt(n).
proof: Exact Schur reduction gives direct_sum_j P_j tau_(j,v). Every decoded branch factors through dimension Q, so its Kraus operators and Choi vectors have rank/Schmidt number at most Q. A covariant spin-score argument plus a Schmidt-rank projector/energy bound yields e>=c*r/Q, including arbitrary output-sector transitions. For the upper, on spin j use F=diag((1-k/Q)_+) in occupation k=j-m, s=Tr F^2=(Q+1)(2Q+1)/(6Q), and Phi_j(X)=(2j+1)/s integral (U F U*)X(U F U*) dU. Its commutator energy is E=Q^-2 sum_(k=1)^Q k(2j-k+1), so E/s<=6j/Q and 1-lambda_1=E/[2s*j*(j+1)]. The full trace-norm thermal-series double-commutator estimate gives T(Phi_j(tau_(j,v)),tau_(j,v))<=3/(2Q)*(beta+beta^2*j/3)*exp(beta*j), beta=2 atanh(r). Exact Schur-weight bounds and unbiased-binomial moments average this to O(c1*r/Q). Finite Euler/Gauss quadrature realizes the Haar channel with O(n^3) total classical outcomes.
supplied_inputs: n and known radius r, or public radius envelope c1/sqrt(n)
whole-state density reconstruction in worst-case half trace
maximum branch dimension Q; every retained input-dependent register is charged
costs: The lower allows arbitrarily many classical labels but limits each quantum branch to Q. The explicit upper has O(n^3) finite classical outcomes, at most Q quantum dimension per outcome, and total direct-sum dimension D<=O(Q*n^3). This does not optimize D. Exact algebraic quadrature, gates, runtime, Schur implementation, finite control precision and fresh output preparation are separate.
baseline: At Q=1 this recovers the EB Theta(r) floor. The exact Schur-cutoff code has a smaller total-D upper at a specified epsilon but does not give a branch-dimension optimum.
falsifier: A fixed-Q full-state code with e=o(r), an allowed rank-Q channel violating the Choi score converse, a sign/factor error in the spin flip, or a failure of the full trace-norm thermal-series bound.
